b1n0-0.text: Two-step shows its error state: the code boxes turn rose and the message says what to do. Five wrong tries lock sign-in for 15 minutes and email the user.

b1n0-1.text: Invitations show the organization, role and what the role can approve before the person sets a password. Finance and MD roles must set up two-step.

b1n1-0.text: Customer sign-in uses the developer’s own brand, not Vento’s navy. Buyers sign in with a one-time code by WhatsApp, SMS or email, so there is no password to forget from abroad.

b1t2.text: No access, not found, errors, offline, session

b1n2-0.text: 403 names the people who can grant access and sends the request to their Approvals. 500 shows a reference to quote and confirms what was saved.

b1n2-1.text: Offline: the banner sits above the page and rows say “Waiting to sync”. Money going out and approvals pause while offline.

b1n3-0.text: Repeated alerts are grouped (6 receipts → one line). Security alerts are always on and can’t be muted.

b2n0-0.text: Unit detail tabs: Overview, Activity (before → after, who approved), Price & status history.

b2n0-1.text: Bulk create never edits existing units; clashes are listed and skipped.

b2n0-2.text: Price list: “Schedule next phase” opens the dialog; new prices need Finance approval.

b2n1-0.text: Duplicate check runs on phone and email as you type. “Create anyway” asks for a reason and is logged. Lead detail is unchanged from the Desktop page.

b2n1-1.text: One contact can hold several roles. Approvals skip anyone with a conflict (e.g. the salesperson who sold to a contractor’s director).

b2n2-0.text: Reschedule shows old and new side by side and the requester’s “Waiting for approval by Finance” state.

b2n3-0.text: Refund lines quote the contract clause they come from, so the buyer and approver see the same basis.

b2n4-0.text: Commission is earned per cleared receipt and shows WHT at 5% before payment. The list is on the Desktop page.

b3n0-0.text: Reversing never deletes: it adds an opposite entry. The person who recorded a receipt can’t approve its reversal.

b3n1-0.text: WHT is worked out on the amount before VAT, using the rule in Statutory rules, and doubled automatically if the vendor has no TIN.

b3n2-0.text: Statements tabs: trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow. Figures are illustrative but the trial balance balances.

b4n0-0.text: Boundary: draw on the map or type beacons from the survey plan (Minna datum, UTM 31N). On a phone, walk the boundary and capture each beacon by GPS.

b4n0-1.text: Clearing an encumbrance needs evidence and two approvals; sales unblock only after the second.

b4n1-0.text: An expired COREN or CORBON registration blocks new contracts and large payments, with a warning 30 days before.

b4n2-0.text: The same four-step indicator appears on each screen so people know where an order is.

b5n0-0.text: One layout for every document: letterhead in the developer’s brand, reference and date, title, key-facts table, numbered clauses, signature blocks, verify link. These replace the two earlier letters on the Desktop page.

b5n0-1.text: Legal wording is a placeholder for your lawyers to replace.

b5n1-0.text: Single column, 600 px, so the same email works on a phone. Approvals never happen from email.

b5n2-0.text: Each is an approved template with quick-reply buttons. Replies land in the buyer’s conversation in Vento.

b6n0-0.text: Proposed only where nothing in the design system fitted; the reason is on each card.

b6n1-0.text: New settings pages use a left sub-navigation (new component: settings nav). The older Roles, Security and AI pages still use the tab row and should move to it.

b6n1-1.text: Statutory rates are sourced and dated, but must be confirmed by your finance team before go-live.

b6n2-0.text: Staff-only console with its own label in the sidebar so nobody mistakes it for a customer workspace. Support access is read-only and logged.

dn0-0.text: Needs attention is the MD’s inbox: every item carries the one action that resolves it, so the dashboard ends in a decision.

dn0-1.text: The project switcher only appears on screens about one project. Home is cross-entity, so it shows the entity switcher alone.

dn1-0.text: An encumbrance shows in three places on purpose: the list badge, the banner on the parcel, and blocked units in Sales. A court order has to stop a sale wherever one could start.

dn1-1.text: Uploading a document of a type that already exists adds a version instead of a new file, so the vault never forks.

dn2-0.text: Gantt-lite puts plan and actual in one bar; only late phases get colour. Budget bars carry a budget marker so overruns read without numbers.

dn2-1.text: Milestones show which buyer stage payments they trigger, linking construction progress to cash.

dn3-0.text: Available units carry the action colour (violet outline); status colours stay for sold, reserved and blocked. Filters dim non-matching units instead of hiding them, so each block keeps its shape.

dn3-1.text: The subscription sheet pins total, deposit and first due date under every step. Diaspora plans stay fixed in the buyer’s currency with the ₦ equivalent beside it.

dn3-2.text: New buyers can be added inside the flow; country of residence sets the diaspora tag and which currencies the plan offers.

dn3-3.text: New buyers can be added inside the flow; country of residence sets the diaspora tag and which currencies the plan offers.

dn4-0.text: Receipts apply oldest-due-first and show each instalment’s new status before you confirm. The confirm button states the amount in both currencies.

dn4-1.text: FX is locked to the CBN rate; editing asks for a reason and tags the line “Edited”. Choosing cash over ₦5m turns the button into “send to AML review”: the receipt is held, not refused.

dn5-0.text: Letters come from the Documents templates, filled from the subscription. The offer letter states the hold deadline; the allocation letter says plainly that it does not transfer title.

dn6-0.text: Letters come from the Documents templates, filled from the subscription. The offer letter states the hold deadline; the allocation letter says plainly that it does not transfer title.

dn7-0.text: Payroll reads gross → statutory deductions → net per entity, then what changed since last month and exactly what approval triggers. Approval is the only irreversible step, so it is the only one with a confirm dialog.

dn7-1.text: Figures reconcile across screens: Parkview’s ₦1.27bn cash is its four bank accounts; its PAYE in Finance matches the payroll run.

dn8-0.text: Each role gets its own home, a sidebar with only its modules, and its own four mobile tabs. Admins can preview any role from the user menu.

rt0.text: Role homes — each role starts on its own work queue

rn0-0.text: Every role home has the same anatomy: four numbers that matter to that role, a queue sorted by due date then impact, and two panels specific to the job. The MD home is the executive home on the Desktop page.

rn1-0.text: Queue items tick off with Undo. In Play, open the user menu → Preview as role to jump between homes.

mn0-0.text: MD tabs: Home · Approvals · Projects · Reports. Approving money asks for confirmation; reminders are instant with Undo.

mn1-0.text: Lists become cards on phones; filters become a scrolling chip row; the main action sits in a sticky bar above the tabs.

mn2-0.text: Site diary in under 30 seconds: location, yesterday’s worker count and common phrases are prefilled, every target is ≥44px, and entries save offline with a visible sync queue.

mn2-1.text: Material requests under the PM’s ₦5m limit go straight to purchasing; the sheet says so before sending.

mn3-0.text: Sales: tap a unit for a sheet with price in ₦, USD and GBP, start a subscription or share the brochure on WhatsApp.

mn6-0.text: Voice diary: hold to talk, then check every field before saving. “Type it instead” is always one tap away.

mn7-0.text: Buyer portal is a separate light surface under the developer’s name. Bank transfer shows the account and a reference so payments match automatically.

mn7-1.text: Buyers with more than one unit switch between them from the header.

cn0-0.text: Approving never needs a second confirm: the button already names the effect. Rejecting needs a comment. Your own requests show as “This is your own request” and can only be cancelled.

cn0-1.text: Timelines show who, what, before → after, and who approved it, on every record.

cn1-0.text: Nothing saves until Import. Errors are fixed in the preview table, one click each. Undo removes exactly what that import added, for 7 days.

cn2-0.text: Plot colours reuse the status palette: violet outline = available (an action), amber reserved, blue paying, emerald fully paid, rose overdue. Filters dim rather than hide.

cn3-0.text: Duplicate leads aren’t blocked: the agent can still submit, and ownership is decided by a person. The digest fits six lines on WhatsApp.

an0-0.text: Off by default. Each feature has its own switch and cost estimate. At the limit AI pauses and every form works manually.

an1-0.text: One marker, the star + “AI”, sits on anything AI produced. Suggestions sit on a faint violet surface until a person accepts them.

an1-1.text: Ask Vento always says what it’s based on (“14 subscriptions you have access to”) and how it found them. Actions it offers still go through review.

an2-0.text: Drafts are never sent or published automatically. A flag is a question, not an accusation; each one needs a person and a note.

an3-0.text: These are the same screens as on the Desktop page with AI switched on from the user menu. With AI off they look exactly like the originals.

kn0.text: Dark versions keep their links inside dark mode, so Play stays dark. Buyer portal, receipt, letters and board pack stay light on purpose: they are documents people print or forward.

n-s0.text: Type: Poppins for headings and the brand mark; Inter for body and every table, with tabular figures. Inter’s taller x-height and true tnum digits hold up in dense ₦ columns where Poppins’ geometric numerals blur.

n-s1.text: Brand violet #7677FB is for focus, selection and charts. Button fills and links use #5B5CE0 because white on #7677FB is only 3.6:1. Status text uses the darker shade of each status colour so badges pass 4.5:1.

n-s2.text: Every list uses the same five states. The offline banner says what is cached, what is queued and that nothing is lost.

t-b.text: Board pack — A4 landscape, export “All artboards (.pdf)”
